entries.title: Anthropic Economic Index: New building blocks for understanding AI use
entries.summary: Adds observed AI-usage evidence to the exposure stack and motivates the repo's task-primitives sidecar.
entries.limitations: Observed Claude usage is not a full labour-market census and is still a platform-specific measure.
entries.repo_notes: Active live source in the V4.2 ensemble and a major input to the future task-native direction.

entries.title: Labor market impacts of AI: A new measure and early evidence
entries.summary: Separates theoretical capability from observed exposure and emphasizes that early labour effects remain limited.
entries.limitations: Uses US outcome data and a platform-linked usage measure, so it still needs Singapore-specific interpretation.
entries.repo_notes: Primary candidate reference for promoting the shadow model beyond readiness-only governance.

entries.title: Task-Completion Time Horizons of Frontier AI Models
entries.summary: Tracks the current task-duration horizons of frontier models and offers a capability input for scenario calibration.
entries.limitations: The benchmark is model-centric and software-task heavy, so it is not a direct occupation impact measure.
entries.repo_notes: Useful for the forecast layer, not for the core structural score.

entries.title: AI, Productivity, and Work Quality
entries.summary: Adds evidence that AI can change both output quantity and work quality, reinforcing the need for occupation-specific augmentation priors.
entries.limitations: Experimental and workflow-specific evidence still needs careful translation into occupation-level scoring.
entries.repo_notes: Useful as a V5.1 calibration reference rather than as a direct V4.x score ingredient.

entries.title: Artificial Intelligence and the Labor Market
entries.summary: Shows that mean exposure and concentration of exposure in a few tasks can have different labour-demand implications.
entries.limitations: The repo uses a simplified shadow-model concentration buffer rather than the paper's full firm-task empirical setting.
entries.repo_notes: Primary scientific justification for publishing task exposure concentration as its own field and using it in the shadow model.

entries.title: Generative AI and Jobs: A Refined Global Index of Occupational Exposure
entries.summary: Adds a recent global occupational exposure measure aligned to international occupation codes.
entries.limitations: Still a global exposure measure rather than a Singapore outcome model.
entries.repo_notes: Included because its ISCO alignment improves crosswalk robustness for the ensemble.

entries.title: Large Language Models, Small Labor Market Effects
entries.summary: Finds small early labour-market effects from chatbot adoption despite meaningful task restructuring, supporting conservative near-term risk shrinkage.
entries.limitations: The study is Denmark-specific and examines early effects; longer-run displacement remains unresolved.
entries.repo_notes: Supports the repo's choice to keep structural risk separate from near-term or realised-risk interpretations.

entries.title: Making AI Count: The Next Measurement Frontier
entries.summary: Argues that AI measurement should become more granular, task-based, and outcome-focused than current official statistics.
entries.limitations: This is a measurement agenda rather than an occupation-scoring formula.
entries.repo_notes: Best reference for the repo's longer-run shift from heuristic confidence toward richer uncertainty and task-native measurement.

entries.title: Navigating the Jagged Technological Frontier
entries.summary: Highlights that AI gains are jagged across tasks and expertise levels rather than smooth across a whole occupation.
entries.limitations: Provides strong augmentation evidence but still within constrained experimental settings.
entries.repo_notes: Supports the repo direction of modelling augmentation as its own construct rather than as a mirror image of automation.

entries.title: The Rapid Adoption of Generative AI
entries.summary: Documents that workplace generative-AI adoption is fast, supporting a separate adoption layer in forecast models.
entries.limitations: Adoption speed alone does not identify realised labour displacement or productivity effects.
entries.repo_notes: Used to justify separating structural pressure from near-term realised-risk proxies.

entries.title: Exposure to Artificial Intelligence and Occupational Mobility: A Cross-country Analysis
entries.summary: Suggests that mobility responses to AI pressure follow structured pathways rather than generic occupational distance rules.
entries.limitations: Cross-country evidence informs the transition design, but the repo still needs a Singapore-specific mobility dataset.
entries.repo_notes: Guides the schema for observed transition priors and future ranking logic in the transition layer.

entries.title: O*NET Database 29.1
entries.summary: Provides the task statements, technology skills, and job-zone context used for explanation and task matching.
entries.limitations: O*NET is US-based and enters the Singapore product mainly as explanatory or crosswalk context.
entries.repo_notes: Not a direct structural-score input, but essential for the supporting task layer and future task-native scoring.

entries.title: US BLS Employment Projections 2024-2034
entries.summary: Provides the external benchmark used for convergent validation and for the BLS-weighted proxy employment field.
entries.limitations: This is US evidence and should not be interpreted as Singapore occupation outcome truth.
entries.repo_notes: Lives in the repo as both a validation benchmark and a clearly labeled external proxy.

entries.title: Generative AI at Work
entries.summary: Shows large heterogeneous productivity effects from AI assistance in a specific workflow, supporting separate augmentation modelling.
entries.limitations: The effect size is workflow-specific and should not be generalized into a universal augmentation constant.
entries.repo_notes: Candidate reference for replacing a single structural augmentation heuristic with workflow-aware priors.

entries.title: GPTs are GPTs: An Early Look at the Labor Market Impact Potential of Large Language Models
entries.summary: Frames LLM exposure around task feasibility and time-saving potential rather than broad automation narratives.
entries.limitations: The paper is early and US-oriented, and it does not by itself provide Singapore labour-market calibration.
entries.repo_notes: Used as a reference for the repo's future task-native model direction, not as a direct live source key.

entries.title: GPTs are GPTs: An Early Look at the Labor Market Impact Potential of Large Language Models
entries.summary: Provides the GPT-oriented exposure source used as one leg of the live exposure ensemble.
entries.limitations: Like other exposure indices, it measures capability overlap rather than realised displacement.
entries.repo_notes: Kept in the live ensemble because it adds an LLM-specific construct not covered by AIOE alone.

entries.title: Labor Market Exposure to AI: Cross-country Differences and Distributional Implications
entries.summary: Provides the complementarity framework that the repo operationalises as the human bottleneck layer.
entries.limitations: Designed as a broad labour-exposure framing rather than a Singapore occupation-level calibrated outcome model.
entries.repo_notes: Directly tied to the theta-based bottleneck implementation in the current scorer.

entries.title: Occupational, industry, and geographic exposure to artificial intelligence: A novel dataset and its potential uses
entries.summary: Provides the published AIOE occupation exposure dataset used as a baseline source in the ensemble.
entries.limitations: Measures theoretical exposure rather than realised AI use or job outcomes.
entries.repo_notes: Tied directly to the live AIOE source key and still used in the canonical exposure ensemble.

entries.title: A Method to Link Advances in Artificial Intelligence to Occupational Abilities
entries.summary: Introduces the task-ability linkage approach that underpins modern AI-exposure measurement.
entries.limitations: Provides the conceptual bridge from AI capabilities to work content, but not current observed usage or Singapore-specific outcomes.
entries.repo_notes: Referenced as the foundational exposure framework behind later AIOE-style occupation measures.
